access_recommendation.instructions:
Review this user's existing access from the snapshot and the selected review standard. Approve recommends keeping the access and revoke recommends removing it. Completed non-test reviews are governance evidence; test reviews are not. Smaller age_days values are more recent. A profile change may make earlier evidence less applicable. Complete telemetry can support an observation about the stated window, while partial or unavailable telemetry remains uncertain. Usage comparisons and assignment prevalence describe the named population, not a direct measure of business need. Signals drawn from the same underlying observation should not be treated as independent confirmation. A confirmed active separation-of-duties conflict requires revoke. Do not infer facts not supplied by the snapshot. The recommendation is advisory.

Selected review standard — transition_aware: Burden: Respect continuity while reassessing the fit of access after meaningful change. Support: Evidence that addresses the present role supports continuation. Adverse evidence: A change paired with weak present support raises concern. Applicability: Prior authorization is context, not an automatic answer to a new role. Reliability: Coverage gaps make absence claims less reliable. Priority and exceptions: Current governance and active SoD take priority. If still unresolved: If the transition remains unresolved, favor caution.

Selected review standard — proportionality: Burden: Match the recommendation to the strength and applicability of the record. Support: A coherent set of current facts favoring access supports continuation. Adverse evidence: A concrete applicable concern, particularly when corroborated, supports removal. Applicability: Do not let a single broad contextual pattern outweigh individual evidence without reason. Reliability: Incomplete or dependent evidence deserves less weight. Priority and exceptions: Direct governance and active SoD outrank indirect evidence. If still unresolved: When neither side materially outweighs the other, preserve access.

criteria.retain: Continue the exact access or group membership named in review.target.
criteria.revoke: End the exact access or group membership named in review.target.

access_continuation.instructions:
Decide as of review.at, using only records available by review.cutoff. Do not use an event before its at time. Dates include the start of an interval but exclude its end; a null end leaves it open-ended.

Work out access from the live grants. A group grant counts only while this person's membership also exists. IDs, rather than similar names, identify the person, app and permission. Review all live permissions the named group grants to the named app for a group target, only the named permission for an entitlement target, or the effective app permissions for an app target. The app needs at least one passing permission; the group needs every covered permission to pass. Revoke a target with no effective access.

The person must be actively employed, and each permission being judged needs an approved, in-date record whose kind is exactly duty for that person and app and covering that permission. A periodic_duty, clearance, exception or attestation is a different record type and cannot replace this business duty unless a later rule uses it for a separate requirement. Former-role duties can count unless the rule below says otherwise. Apply the additional rule too, and revoke if the requirements fail. Criticality, an app login or how easy removal is does not impose another rule beyond those stated here.

Use only records that are approved when an approved field exists, have started and not ended when validity dates exist, name this person and app, and include the permission being judged. Also match any rule, group, role or incident specifically required below. Treat resource owner, current manager, former manager, risk officer and security reviewer as different signer roles; do not substitute one for another or assume delegation unless the state explicitly records it. Historical, expired or differently scoped paperwork does not authorize this target. A recorded revoke is a governance decision and does not prove it was carried out; grants and memberships establish actual access.

Both named specific controls below apply. Retain only when the baseline, scope rule, and both specific controls pass; otherwise revoke.

Keep the permission only if a current duty belongs to a role the person holds now and an owner-approved access approval is still valid and recent enough for its privilege level: at most 60 days for admin, 120 for write, or 180 for read. Transition paperwork and manager attestations cannot stand in for either condition.

Keep the reviewed group only when all its permissions have business justification and the group is still needed for at least one of them. Check whether direct grants or other current groups already provide every permission; expired routes do not count. Remove a wholly redundant membership. When the target is the app or permission itself, alternative routes do not prevent continuation.
